facts.statement: Each merge run uses one format (technical-writing, code-review, or notes) and one weight; mixed batches are split into separate runs.
Primary docs (written entirely by the author) get weight 1.0; secondary docs (author's text mixed with others') get weight 0.3.

New private terms are listed, shown to the user, and appended to ~/.config/writing-in-voice/denylist.txt (creating file and parent directory if missing); they are never written anywhere inside either skill directory.
All profile edits happen in a staged copy ($STAGE, outside both skill directories, made with rm -rf $STAGE && cp -R $SKILL_DIR $STAGE); SKILL_DIR is never edited directly before approval.

Layer 1 numbers merge by running scripts/merge_profile.py --skill-dir $STAGE --format <format> --weight <w> --docs <paths>, which updates layer1-<format>.json exactly and regenerates layer1-<format>.md; --dry-run previews the metric shifts.
Layers 2-4 and the shape card are edited by hand in STAGE, comparing the new docs against layer2-<format>.md, layer4-<format>.md, layer3-substance.md, and shapes/<format>.md.
A pattern, tic, stance, or layout rule is added only when it appears in at least two of the new docs, or in one new doc plus existing profile evidence.
Every new prose entry is written as a generic paraphrase and never quotes the source; only short stock tics (e.g. "IIUC", "lgtm") may be quoted.
Profile entries never cite source files, doc IDs, PR numbers, dates, or people.
Strengthen or reword an existing entry instead of adding a near-duplicate.
Every illustration is an invented example on a neutral topic (caches, queues, file exports, test flakiness).
Every new Layer 3 stance is tagged grounded (stated directly in a doc) or extrapolated (inferred across docs), and the tag summary line is updated.

When the shape card changed, exemplars/<format>.md is rewritten as a new synthetic piece on a neutral topic following the updated card and validated with validate_voice.py until it exits 0 with every Layer 1 metric in range.

The gate runs check_leaks.py (must exit 0), the unit tests (must pass), and wc -l over SKILL.md, shapes/<format>.md, exemplars/<format>.md, layer{1,2,4}-<format>.md, layer3-substance.md, and negative-list.md; the combined total must stay under 500 lines; the run stops on any failure, and a leak is fixed by rewriting the offending entry in STAGE then rerunning the gate.
Nothing is copied back until the user approves the complete diff -ru $SKILL_DIR $STAGE -x __pycache__ output.
Promotion is rsync -a --exclude __pycache__ $STAGE/ $SKILL_DIR/, followed by rerunning the leak checker against SKILL_DIR with the same --source paths, which must exit 0.

The merge is permanent: the profile stores only weighted means, stdevs, and total weight, so a merged doc cannot be subtracted later and ingesting the same path twice double-counts it; ask before re-ingesting any path.

check_leaks.py only knows what it is given: its overlap check covers only this run's --source paths and its term check covers only the deny-list, so new private names must be collected and deny-listed before merging.
A missing deny-list is a warning, not a hard stop: check_leaks.py prints a warning and skips the term check, so recreate the file from the user's terms rather than running without one.
A paraphrase that keeps the source's distinctive word order trips the 8-word overlap check; rewrite from the pattern, not from the sentence.
Zeta word lists were removed on purpose — they need per-doc presence data the profile does not store and they leaked domain nouns; never reintroduce them.

excluded.reason: restatement of the merge-script and paraphrase facts; covered by their entries
$SKILL_DIR/$STAGE variable definitions restate the staging fact; covered by its entry
restatements of step facts already covered by entries
frontmatter guidance is always out of scope for retrieval testing
